summary:
I want to thank you for the recent large check made up of French reprint royal­ ties, but if I may I’d like at the same time to remind you that several months ago I dis­ cussed with you the fact that the local banks here will not accept large out-of-state checks without sending them back to their originating bank for collection. For a time you were sending all my checks above two or three hundred dollars to me in the form 

358  of certified checks, which the banks here will accept for deposit without question—as you said then, this type of check is as good as cash. 

In particular I am anticipating static from the banks here on the option check for the movie sale of DO ANDROIDS DREAM OF ELECTRIC SHEEP. I doubt if any bank in Orange County would accept it for deposit and let me draw against it without returning it to New York first for collection. So with all due respects, could I request once more that you resume the practice of sending me the larger checks in certified form? The banks here are really nuts, but I don’t want their problems to become mine. Thank you, and again, thank you for the movie sale plus all else. 

Cordially, Philip K. Dick 

Especially the option check 

ITO SCOTT MYERJ 

November 30,
